chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'It is like one who has visited Allah on His Throne.' I asked, 'What is the reward for one who visits any one of you (or one of you)?' He replied, 'It is like one who has visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (specifically to the graves of saints or Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this foundational hadith where Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the physical act of Ziyarah to a metaphysical encounter, equating the visitation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with 'visiting Allah on His Throne.' This reflects the Shia theological concept of the Imams as the ultimate manifestation of Divine presence (Tajalli) and the axis of creation, transforming a ritual act into a direct spiritual connection with the Divine Reality. The comparison to visiting the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.) for other Imams underscores their unique status as the successors and living proofs of Prophethood.
